text: Overlook's database is now provisioned, secured, and protected by a tested failover group. All of that still depends on someone manually running checks and remembering to run them — exactly the problem Lesson 1 described, just moved one chapter later. This chapter builds the automation the board actually asked for.

SQL Server Management Studio is a GUI, built for a human clicking through menus one server at a time. dbatools is a free, open-source PowerShell module, purpose-built for exactly the repetitive, unattended administration work a GUI was never designed for.

Invoke-DbaQuery runs real T-SQL against a server and hands back the results as real PowerShell objects. Notice it connects to overlook-fg dot database dot windows dot net — Chapter 4's failover group listener endpoint, not a specific server name. A script hardcoded to one server would break after a failover; this one keeps working no matter which region is currently primary.
Because the output is a real object collection, it plugs directly into ordinary PowerShell filtering. Next lesson combines several checks like this one into a single, real health-check routine.
